title: Annotatio II open §.I: De Consubstantiatione — from verbal fight to real-presence debate
pass_a_gloss: ANNOTATION II. On Consubstantiation, comprising a little Compendium of its History at the Author’s pp. 34 and 36 at the end. §. I. And in the Eucharistic war, from the verbal rhetorical skirmish about the interpretation of Christ’s words This is my body — proper or improper — it has come to a real Debate about the presence of Christ’s body itself in the Sacred Supper, or rather about the mode of presence.
pass_b_english: Annotatio II opens On Consubstantiation — a short history at Author pp. 34 and 36 fin.
§.I: the Eucharistic war has moved from the verbal fight over whether This is my body is proper or improper to a real debate on Christ’s bodily presence in the Supper — or rather its mode.
source_text: ANNOTATIO II. De Consubstantiatione, Historia ejus Compendiolum complexa ad pag. Aut. 34. & 36. in fin. §. I. IN atque bello Eucharistico, à velitatione verbali rhetorica, de verborum Christi, hoc est corpus meum, interpretatione, propriâ, an impropriâ, ad realem, de ipsius corporis Christi in Sacra Coena praesentia, seu praesentiae potiùs modo, deventum est Disceptationem.
notes: Annotatio II §.I open; verbal → real presence.
